"which leaves me little time to do my real work. But soon you both will become Master Librarians,
and that will be a big help to me." Jack smiled.
He was going to be a Master Librarian who traveled through time and space.
It was almost too good to believe. "Are you ready to solve another riddle?" asked Morgan.
"Yes," said Jack and Annie together. "Good," said Morgan. "First, you'll need this for research."
research … ” She pulled a book from her robe and handed it to Jack.

Maybe the answer to the riddle is in there.”

“We can’t keep fighting this one, boss!”
She wants her colt,” another said.

Then Sunset showed up all alone,” said Annie.

Jack sneezed as he bounced along into the setting sun.

The wind was cool, almost cold.

Jack saw a campfire at the bottom of the slope.
He saw the horses gathered in a dark clump.
One let out a loud whinny.
“Sounds like she’s tied to a tree,” said Slim.
“I think the rest of the herd are loose.”
“Smiley, you stay here and guard Sunset,” said Slim.

“Then you and Sunset take off, Smiley.”

Yup, about a million, thought Jack.

Maybe now I can ask Slim some questions, thought Jack.

And the band of mustangs galloped after the mare.
He clutched the reins in one hand and the saddle horn in the other.

Dusty cleared the rise in an awkward leap.
Jack started to slip out of the saddle.

Oh, man, thought Jack, this is the end.

It was hard without Slim’s help.

Jack didn’t have time to think about what he was seeing.
He knew it might be his only chance to escape.
Using all his strength, he pulled himself into the saddle.
Dusty took off at full gallop over the prairie.

If he hadn’t come, I never would have gotten away!”

I better take some notes, thought Jack.

He had slept a long time.

He walked over and gave Jack a biscuit and a cup of coffee.
“It’s hard as a rock,” Slim said.
"It's hard as a rock," Slim said, "in bitter as muddy river water.
But a cowboy takes what he can get.”

The book he wrote after he left us!”
